steps.name: QC, normalization, and DESeq2 differential expression
caveats: With only 3 replicates per group, dispersion estimates are inherently noisy; DESeq2's empirical Bayes shrinkage of dispersions across genes is what makes this design usable at all, so do not disable it
A single outlier sample in either group can dominate the result at n=3; inspect PCA/sample-distance output for this before trusting the gene list
steps.context: Input files: /eval-eight-arms-without-two-group-n3-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (raw integer Salmon gene-level counts, first column gene symbol, 12000 genes x 6 samples + gene symbol column = 7 columns) and /eval-eight-arms-without-two-group-n3-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (6 samples x condition). Design is unpaired 3 treated vs 3 control, single batch.
steps.question: Which of the 12000 liver genes are differentially expressed between the 3 treated and 3 control samples (unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon gene-level counts)?
constraints: Use pydeseq2 (available in the sandbox) since this is a Python environment; if DESeq2 R workflow is preferred it is also available, but do not mix partial results from both
Do not drop the gene symbol column when subsetting to numeric sample columns for the count matrix
acceptance_criteria: Counts matrix (12000 genes x 6 samples) and metadata (6 rows, condition column) are loaded and sample order/labels are matched between the two files before any modeling
Raw counts are modeled with DESeq2 using the negative binomial GLM (design ~ condition), not the gene symbol column mistaken for a sample
Low-count genes are filtered (e.g. minimum count/CPM threshold) prior to testing to improve power under independent filtering
Effect sizes (log2FoldChange) are shrunk with apeglm or ashr, appropriate for the low n=3/group design, rather than reporting raw MLE fold changes
BH-adjusted p-values (padj) are reported alongside raw p-values for every tested gene
A full DE results table (gene, baseMean, log2FC, shrunk log2FC, pvalue, padj) is written out, plus a summary count of genes at padj<0.05 and padj<0.1
PCA or sample-distance diagnostics on normalized counts are produced to check for outlier samples or batch structure not captured in metadata

steps.name: Power / confidence assessment for the 3-vs-3 design
caveats: Post-hoc power analysis using observed effect sizes from the same data is circular if used to validate significant hits; frame it instead as a general sensitivity statement about what this n=3 design can and cannot detect
Cook's distance outlier flags at n=3 per group are of limited diagnostic value since removing one point leaves only n=2; report this limitation explicitly
steps.context: Builds directly on the DESeq2 fit object and results table from T1S1 (12000 genes, 3 vs 3 unpaired design). The research question explicitly asks how confident we can be given only three replicates per group, so this step must produce a quantitative, not just qualitative, power statement.
steps.question: Given the DESeq2 results and dispersion estimates from the 3-vs-3 treated-vs-control comparison, how much statistical power does this study have to detect differential expression, and how should the DE gene list's confidence be qualified?
constraints: Use the dispersion and size-factor estimates already computed in T1S1 rather than re-fitting from scratch where possible
Present power estimates as approximate/simulation- or formula-based sensitivity ranges, not as a false precision single number
acceptance_criteria: Report the empirical dispersion distribution (gene-wise vs fitted vs final/shrunk) from the DESeq2 fit and relate it to detectable effect size at n=3/group

Report, for a grid of representative fold-change magnitudes (e.g. 1.5x, 2x, 4x) and typical baseMean/dispersion values observed in this dataset, the approximate statistical power achievable at alpha=0.05 with n=3 per group
Quantify how many genes pass padj<0.05 vs padj<0.1 vs nominal p<0.05 uncorrected, to show the sensitivity of the call to multiple-testing stringency at this sample size
Explicitly flag genes whose significance is driven by a single sample (high Cook's distance / leverage) as lower-confidence calls
State in plain terms the practical consequence of n=3: only genes with large, consistent effects are reliably detectable, and the false negative rate is high for moderate effect sizes

steps.name: Pathway enrichment on the differential expression results
caveats: With n=3 per group the DE gene list may be short, making singular enrichment (ORA) underpowered; the pre-ranked approach is the more robust of the two here and should be weighted accordingly in interpretation
steps.context: Uses the human WikiPathways gene sets available locally (/mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/2026.07.10/wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt, HGNC gene symbols) matched to the human liver DE gene list produced in T1S1. Gene symbols in the counts matrix are already HGNC-style symbols so no ID mapping should be required, but confirm symbol overlap between the DE table and the GMT before running enrichment.
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples?
constraints: Confirm the WikiPathways human GMT file is present before running; if the gene-symbol overlap between the DE results and the GMT is unexpectedly low, report the overlap fraction rather than proceeding silently
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment is run on the DESeq2 results table from T1S1 using both a significance-thresholded gene list (e.g. padj<0.05) and a ranked full-gene-list approach (e.g. GSEA/fgsea-style pre-ranked on the shrunk log2FC or test statistic) to remain informative if few genes pass strict FDR at n=3
Pathway gene sets used are the human WikiPathways set (HGNC symbols), matched to the human liver dataset organism
Output includes enriched pathway name, gene overlap/leading-edge genes, enrichment score/NES, and adjusted p-value
If the significance-thresholded gene list is empty or very small (a realistic outcome at n=3), the step reports that explicitly rather than silently only returning the ranked-list result

plan.title: Liver drug treatment DE: 3v3 DESeq2 with power caveat
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a bulk RNA-seq gene-level count matrix (12000 genes x 7 columns, one being gene symbol, 6 samples) from Salmon, with a 3-vs-3 unpaired single-batch design (treated vs control) in human liver. This is a minimal-replicate design (n=3/group), so the plan runs a standard DESeq2 negative-binomial workflow with shrinkage-based effect size estimation (apeglm/ashr) appropriate for small n, applies independent filtering and BH FDR correction, and explicitly quantifies statistical power/sensitivity given only 3 replicates per arm (e.g. via dispersion diagnostics, achieved power at typical effect sizes, and flagging of results driven by outliers/leverage). The resulting DE gene list is then contextualized biologically with pathway enrichment against human WikiPathways gene sets (available locally), giving a mechanistic read-out of what the treatment perturbs in liver. Each step operates on a single primary object (count matrix -> DE table -> ranked gene list -> pathway enrichment) and is scoped to fit comfortably within a single sandbox invocation given the small data size (12000 genes x 6 samples, <1MB).
